claim: The pinned demonstrations directory contains 19 JSON .traj blobs totaling exactly 1,503,861 bytes.
limitations: Count excludes the adjacent YAML demonstration because this inspection targeted .traj JSON files.

claim: All 19 inspected .traj blobs parse as JSON and their SHA-256 values are recorded without retaining raw content.
limitations: Checksums identify the inspected bytes only at the pinned revision.

claim: Eighteen files expose info.model_stats with tokens_sent, tokens_received, instance_cost, and api_calls; the remaining history-only fixture has no model_stats.
limitations: Field presence does not imply measurement validity.

claim: Every tokens_sent, tokens_received, and instance_cost value in the 18 model_stats objects is zero, despite non-empty trajectories.
limitations: The creation mechanism for the placeholder zeros is not documented inside each file.

claim: The demonstration token and cost zeros must not be normalized as measured zero-token inference and cannot influence numerical routing priors.
limitations: Applies to the inspected revision and fixture set, not every SWE-agent trajectory release.

claim: Three replay/function-calling files report api_calls values 11, 11, and 13 while token and cost fields remain zero; provider-request semantics are therefore unverified.
limitations: The fields may describe replay operations rather than fresh provider requests.

claim: All 19 trajectories contain explicit thought fields, so a metadata-only derivative avoids publishing unnecessary reasoning-like text.
limitations: This finding concerns field presence; raw thought content was not reproduced.

claim: Eighteen files report exit_status submitted, but none exposes an objective verifier result in the inspected trajectory schema.
limitations: A companion evaluation artifact outside these files could exist; it was not part of this bounded corpus.

claim: Four replay configurations name gpt-4o and one names replay; fourteen files have no safe structured model identifier.
limitations: A replay configuration name does not prove that fresh inference occurred or identify a dated model snapshot.

claim: The repository's MIT license supports a derived metadata fixture with attribution, but licensing alone does not justify republishing full prompts, observations, or thought text.
limitations: Not legal advice; underlying task material can have additional provenance considerations.
